# Temple Scroll Column 40 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 40 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**40:1** Measure three thousand cubits outward from the temple city in every direction — this is the city's sacred boundary.

**40:2** Beyond this boundary you may build homes and settlements.

**40:3** But do not build anything within the boundary zone — it is holy ground.

**40:4** This boundary shall separate the holy from the ordinary, the clean from the unclean.

**40:5** Observe this boundary as a permanent law for all future generations.

**40:6** Whenever someone dies inside a house, that house becomes unclean for seven days.

**40:7** Any uncovered container — one without a tight lid — becomes unclean as well.

**40:8** Everything in the house becomes unclean, and anyone who enters it will be unclean for seven days.

**40:9** On the first day the person must wash his clothes and bathe. On the third day he must be sprinkled with purification water.

**40:10** On the seventh day he must be sprinkled again, wash his clothes, and bathe. By evening he will be clean.

**40:11** Everything the dead person touched — every container, piece of clothing, leather item, and tool — must be purified.

**40:12** Wooden items shall be washed; clay pots shall be smashed; and items made of copper, bronze, tin, lead, or iron shall be purified with the purification water.

**40:13** Anyone who touches a dead body and fails to go through purification defiles the LORD's dwelling place.

**40:14** That person shall be expelled from Israel, because purification water was never sprinkled on him, and he remains unclean.

**40:15** His uncleanness stays with him, and anyone who touches him will be unclean until evening.

**40:16** Teach the people of Israel all these rules. They must follow them carefully so they do not defile My temple or My city where I dwell.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column defines the sacred buffer zone around the temple city and gives detailed instructions for handling corpse contamination. The purification process closely follows Numbers 19. The material-specific vessel rules distinguish between porous clay (must be destroyed) and non-porous materials (can be purified).*
